is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports sequencing of the sodium channel gene (VGSC) to detect kdr mutations (page 2, 4, 6, 7). Specifically, it investigates the 1014 codon (page 4, 6, 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 4 provides summary statistics for polymorphism at the sodium channel gene, including sample sizes (N=38 total, 12 susceptible, 26 resistant) and haplotype counts (page 6).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Tororo District, Uganda (page 2, Materials and Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original field collections and laboratory analyses (page 1-7).

sub_country_location.evidence: Tororo District, Uganda (page 2, Materials and Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were carried out in April and November 2009 (page 2, Materials and Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection and forced-egg laying method for An. funestus in Tororo, Uganda, in 2009.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data, including bioassay results and genotype summary statistics, are provided in the main text tables.

assessment.summary: This study reports on the insecticide susceptibility and resistance mechanisms of Anopheles funestus from Tororo, Uganda. The authors found resistance to pyrethroids and DDT, but susceptibility to bendiocarb, malathion, and dieldrin. They performed biochemical assays, RT-PCR for P450 genes, and sequenced the VGSC gene (1014 codon) to investigate resistance mechanisms, finding no kdr mutations but evidence of metabolic resistance.
